consistency_rules: Death tally: UCDP best estimate (all violence types: state-based, non-state, one-sided), summed over the countries where the named event takes place, from UCDP GED via Our World in Data (geolocated); 2025 uses UCDP Candidate Events (preliminary). Another tally (official, EM-DAT, WHO, peer-reviewed study) is used only where UCDP does not cover the event: natural disasters, epidemics, heat, famine. IBC, ACLED, NST, SOHR and Wikipedia tallies are not used for any conflict UCDP covers, even where both builders agreed on them.

Criminal violence (Mexico) counts only where a conflict dataset lists it with >= 10,000 deaths in the year: UCDP non-state conflicts between cartels, so Mexico counts 2018-2024 and not in 2010, 2011, 2016, 2017 or 2025. Homicide statistics do not count.

Heat mortality counts only where a peer-reviewed estimate for that year exists: Russia 2010 (Shaposhnikov et al. 2014, about 11,000 in Moscow alone), Europe 2022, 2023, 2024 (Nature Medicine). Europe 2025 rests on a rapid non-peer-reviewed study and is dropped.
Residual COVID-19 counts while WHO-reported COVID-19 deaths in the year are >= 10,000: kept for 2020-2025.

Review criterion: the event must be named as a shock or main downside development in the executive summary or chapter 1 overview of the IMF WEO (April Y+1 or January update) or the World Bank GEP (January Y+1). A mention only in a country forecast or a special feature does not count. Upside developments (AI investment surge) do not count. A commodity price collapse counts as a shock because the reviews treat it as one.

Agreed events are still tested against these rules; an agreed event that fails is recorded as dropped (in_builders A,B). Neither-builder events found by applying the same UCDP rule across years are added as kept with in_builders [] (Ethiopia 2020; Mexico 2022-2024).
Duplicates: one development split into two entries by a builder is merged into one event (Brazil/Russia recessions 2015 into the commodity slump).
